From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: seance and Séance

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • seance

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French séance (“sitting, session”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (US) IPA(key): /ˈseɪˌɑns/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɑːns

Noun

[edit]

séance (plural séances)

  1. A ceremony where people try to communicate with the spirits of dead people, usually led by a medium.
    • 1936, Rollo Ahmed, The Black Art, London: Long, page 231:
      [B]ut only too often séances degenerate into pure sorcery or necromancy, attracting all kinds of undeveloped and earth-bound entities.
  2. (dated) The sitting of an assembly to discuss a matter.

Translations

[edit]
a ceremony where people try to communicate with the spirits

  • Bulgarian: сеанс (bg) m (seans)

  • German: Séance (de) f
  • Hebrew: העלאה באוב f

  • Hungarian: szeánsz (hu)

  • Italian: seduta spiritica f

Verb

[edit]

séance (third-person singular simple present séances, present participle séancing, simple past and past participle séanced)

  1. To hold a séance (communication with spirits).

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Neaces, Seneca, acenes, censae, encase, scenae, scæne

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From séant +‎ -ance, possibly corresponding to Latin sedentia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /se.ɑ̃s/
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Homophone: séances
  • Hyphenation: sé‧ance
  • Rhymes: -ɑ̃s

Noun

[edit]

séance f (plural séances)

  1. session

Derived terms

[edit]
  • préséance
  • séance tenante

Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from French séance (“session”), from Latin sedentia.

Noun

[edit]

séance

  1. séance: spiritual meeting

Further reading

[edit]
  • “séance”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016
